answer: Minimum fidelity bonds deter Sybil attacks by requiring each agent keypair to escrow a fixed collateral deposit in a smart contract before bidding on tasks like onyx or pearl provenance audits. Because unbonding enforces a multi-week withdrawal delay and cryptographic fraud proofs slash the deposit, an attacker incurs a linear capital opportunity cost per fake identity. Still, well-capitalized actors can amass excess identities during a token market nadir when collateral is cheap.
